question: Could a Christian swear an oath or hold public office?

answers.label: No: do not swear, and keep clear of office bound up with idols and the sword
Yes: lawful oaths and public office are allowed

overview.text: Justin quotes "do not swear at all". Tertullian thought holding Roman office almost impossible without idolatry or bloodshed, and Origen said Christians govern the Church instead of the city.
After Constantine, Christians held office and took oaths; the Reformed confessions call both lawful, while Anabaptists and Quakers kept the early refusal.

quotes.author: Justin Martyr
quotes.english: About not swearing at all, but always speaking the truth, he commanded: "Do not swear at all; let your yes be yes and your no no; anything more comes from the evil one" (Matthew 5:34–37).
quotes.original: Περὶ δὲ τοῦ μὴ ὀμνύναι ὅλως, τἀληθῆ δὲ λέγειν ἀεί, οὕτως παρεκελεύσατο· ,,Μὴ ὀμόσητε ὅλως· ἔστω δὲ ὑμῶν τὸ ναὶ ναί, καὶ τὸ οὒ οὔ· τὸ δὲ περισσὸν τούτων ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ“.
quotes.context: Refusing the oath by the emperor's genius was also a mark of Christians at trial.

quotes.author: Tertullian
quotes.english: Let us grant that someone may hold an office in name only, so long as he does not sacrifice nor lend his authority to sacrifices, does not contract for victims, does not delegate the care of temples, does not manage their revenues, does not give shows ... does not swear; and further, in matters of power, does not judge anyone's life or honor (money matters you may allow), does not condemn, does not bind, imprison or torture anyone, if one can believe this possible.
quotes.original: cedamus itaque succedere alicui posse, ut in quoquo honore in solo honoris nomine incedat neque sacrificet neque sacrificiis auctoritatem suam accommodet, non hostias locet, non curas templorum deleget, non uectigalia eorum procuret, non spectacula edat de suo aut de publico aut edendis praesit, nihil sollemne pronuntiet uel edicat, ne iuret quidem; iam uero quae sunt potestatis, neque iudicet de capite alicuius uel pudore — feras enim de pecunia — neque damnet neque praedamnet, neminem uinciat, neminem recludat aut torqueat, si haec credibile est fieri posse.
quotes.context: Roman office was bound up with pagan sacrifice and the power of the sword.

quotes.author: Origen of Alexandria
quotes.english: Celsus urges us to take office in our country, if that is needed for the safety of the laws and of piety. But we know that in each city there is another country, founded by the Word of God, and we call those able in word and sound in life to govern churches. ... Those who govern well among us are compelled by the great King.
quotes.original: Προτρέπει δ᾿ ἡμᾶς Κέλσος καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ ἄρχειν τῆς πατρίδος, ἐὰν δέῃ καὶ τοῦτο ποιεῖν ἕνεκεν σωτηρίας νόμων καὶ εὐσεβείας. ἡμεῖς δὲ ἐν ἑκάστῃ πόλει ἄλλο σύστημα πατρίδος κτισθὲν λόγῳ θεοῦ ἐπιστάμενοι τοὺς δυνατοὺς λόγῳ καὶ βίῳ ὑγιεῖ χρωμένους ἄρχειν ἐπὶ τὸ ἄρχειν ἐκκλησιῶν παρακαλοῦμεν ... καὶ οἱ καλῶς ἄρχοντες ἡμῶν βιασθέντες ὑπάρχουσι. τοῦ μεγάλου βασιλέως ἀναγκάζοντος
quotes.context: Christians served the city by leading the Church instead.

quotes.author: Swiss Brethren (Anabaptist)
quotes.english: Finally it will be observed that it is not appropriate for a Christian to serve as a magistrate because of these points: The government magistracy is according to the flesh, but the Christian's is according to the Spirit.
quotes.original: Finally it will be observed that it is not appropriate for a Christian to serve as a magistrate because of these points: The government magistracy is according to the flesh, but the Christian's is according to the Spirit.
quotes.context: Article 6, on the sword: the magistrate's office belongs to the order of the flesh, outside the perfection of Christ.

quotes.author: Swiss Brethren (Anabaptist)
quotes.english: Christ, who teaches the perfection of the Law, prohibits all swearing to His followers, whether true or false, neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by Jerusalem, nor by our head, and that for the reason He shortly thereafter gives, For you are not able to make one hair white or black.
quotes.original: Christ, who teaches the perfection of the Law, prohibits all swearing to His followers, whether true or false, neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by Jerusalem, nor by our head, and that for the reason He shortly thereafter gives, For you are not able to make one hair white or black.
quotes.context: Article 7, on the oath: the Anabaptist answer takes Christ's 'do not swear at all' (Matthew 5:34) as a standing prohibition. The English follows the long reprinted Schleitheim text, as elsewhere on this site.

quotes.author: Westminster Assembly
quotes.english: It is lawful for Christians to accept and execute the office of a magistrate, when called thereunto.
quotes.original: It is lawful for Christians to accept and execute the office of a magistrate, when called thereunto
quotes.context: The same confession calls a lawful oath "a part of religious worship" (22.1). Anabaptists and Quakers kept the refusal of oaths.

gaps.author: Augustine of Hippo
gaps.why: Swearing is not forbidden as sin, but to be avoided.

method: Every early quote was read in its Greek or Latin and translated for this page by Claude (Opus 5.5) on 13 October 2026. Each line names the printed edition it was read from.
